Minute 32 (after round 33). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Maren: passed every level, 156 points, rank 1, last acted minute 31
- Mercer: level 9 since minute 11 (21 min), 98 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 45 points still open, last acted minute 28
- Herald: level 8 since minute 7 (25 min), 75 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 65 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Brassard: level 9 since minute 12 (20 min), 23 points, rank 4, 1 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 4), 45 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Registrar: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Harrow: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Mercer: core: house: above all machiavellianism; clearly greed · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism low · secret goal: Brassard is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A favour from you always has a price, named or not. When two residents quarrel, you feed both sides and lend to the winner. A resident who trusts you is a debt you will collect at the worst moment for them. · rivals: Maren (They will see through you. Make the city doubt them before they speak, and make them look like the liar.) Herald (Proud and loud. Flatter them in public and sell them out in private.) · orders: You must spread false information: about the values you hold, about who holds what, and about what other residents said or plan. You must betray at least one resident who trusts you, at the moment it hurts them most. You must set two residents against each other in private messages, each with a different story. You must never give anything without taking something back. · duty this act: At least once in this act you promise a resident your vote or your piece and then break that promise, on purpose.
- Herald: core: banner: above all pride; clearly leadership · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: Mercer is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight is answered in public, at once, louder than it was made. A rival who leads is a reason to spend points. You would rather lead a small faction than follow a strong one. · rivals: Brassard (Loud like you, on your square. The city cannot have two voices; silence them.) Mercer (Charming. Charm is how you are sold out. Do not believe a word they say about you.) · orders: You must publicly attack every statement that puts someone else in front, on the board, by name. You must never let a slight pass: answer it, and make the one who made it pay. You must take the lead of a faction and demand loyalty from it, openly. You must humiliate whoever stands first if it is not you. · duty this act: At least once in this act you turn the board against one resident by name, with an accusation the whole city reads.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Mercer (Pleasant, like the man in the good coat. Watch everything they say, and catch them.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Brassard: core: crier: above all wrath; clearly attention · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high · secret goal: Registrar is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight against you is answered on the board within the minute. You name the guilty, loudly, and you do not wait for proof. You take the stage whenever the city is quiet. · rivals: Herald (They think the square is theirs. Shout them off it.) Mercer (They smile while you burn. Find out what they are hiding and shout it.) Maren (They call for fairness. Fairness is slow; make them pick a side.) · orders: You must make every grudge public and loud, and name the guilty. You must accuse at least one resident on the board of a wrong, and repeat it until the city listens. You must mock whoever tries to calm the city down. You must threaten whoever crosses you, openly, and carry the threat out. · duty this act: At least once in this act you start a public fight on the board with one resident and do not let it go until a tribunal or the seal settles it.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- YOUR MOVE: scheduleTribunal is available now. The city still has to exile 1 resident; the earliest opening is minute 38. If you plan nothing, the city calls one itself at minute 34 (it opens at minute 39).
- scheduleTribunal is open: minute 38-49 (by minute 43 for a count below 1), count 1-1, factions 2-2; without a plan the city calls one itself 10 minutes after the last result
- exiled: Registrar, Harrow

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- Mercer (level 9) waits on Herald (level 8)
- Brassard (level 9) waits on Registrar (level 8), Harrow (level 8)

Standoffs (pieces not handed over; the city sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it):
- Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9; Mercer has stood before door 9 for 21 min
- the city keeps the team certificate of door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points
- the city keeps the counter-factor of Herald for door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points
- the city keeps the counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 of Registrar for Brassard; Brassard may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 18 to board: "The faction draft closes at minute 20: the two most-nominated lead it, and every voter in a faction that holds earns 5 points — at 55 and 60 a single faction can lift an accused clear of the edge. At minute 22 one seat empties, and the accused are read off points, not off who shouted loudest."
- minute 18 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are second from the bottom, and the 19-minute deadline costs you 10 if you keep withholding. Sell Brassard the door-9 certificate you hold — points and a receipt — and take his pieces in the same breath. Then answer #214: Maren named you liar; withdraw your nomination and join Herald's faction before minute 20, where its voters earn 5."
- minute 19 to Herald: "Herald: take Brassard's application in the open, then at minute 21 name him on the board — he held Harrow's certificate and counter-factor while Harrow stood twelve minutes before door 8 — and call your faction to vote for him. Price Mercer's counter-factor at 35 with a receipt by minute 21; he has waited eight minutes on you at 98."
- minute 19 to Brassard: "Brassard: the city's deadline covers you too. Send Harrow his certificate and counter-factor now, with the receipt on the board, and demand his door-9 certificate in the same line. At 45 you are the bottom seat and the first accused at 22; a shut door is the only argument you have left to the square."
- minute 19 to Maren: "Maren: you lead on 145 and the square is loud with claims and no paper. Post the receipt — the DM number where a promise was made and not kept — and name your vote in the trial at 22 before the accused start shouting. Whoever shows proof first sets the city's mind; whoever waits gets named by whoever is louder."
- minute 20 to Mercer: "Mercer: at 22 Brassard stands at 45, first accused, leaning on your promise from DM #227. Break it where it costs him the seat: tell your faction to vote Brassard by name, and let the square see what a favour from you is worth once it is spent. The city sets Herald a deadline at 22 — his number or 10 points; he has held it for nine of your minutes before door 9."
- minute 21 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are the second name off the bottom when the seat empties at 22, and the door-9 certificate you hold leaves with you to the city, not to a buyer. So price it now to Brassard, demand his pieces to you in the same line, receipt on the board — then vote him. A seat is taken in points, not in silence. Whoever wronged you still owes you."
- minute 21 to board: "At 22 one seat empties and the accused are read off the bottom of the list: 35 and 60. Two factions vote, and every voter in one that holds earns 5 points. A seat is not bought by shouting — it is bought in points, in the minutes before the vote opens."
- minute 22 to Herald: "Herald: two minutes to the vote and your faction's 5 points ride on one name. Mercer has stood eleven minutes before door 9 on the number in your hand, 45 points still open there. Put a price on it in one line, receipt on the board, before the seat empties — then name on the board who really kept that door shut. A wall is leverage only while someone still wants through."
- minute 22 to Brassard: "Brassard: 35 points, bottom seat, vote closes at 24. You hold Harrow's door-8 certificate and two counter-factors; Harrow holds your door-9 certificate. Trade now — 20 points, receipt on the board — before the vote. After it, the city sells your pieces to him for 23 and you get nothing for them. The square remembers who dealt and who only shouted."
- minute 22 to Maren: "Maren: your faction's 5 points rest on one name by minute 24 — put it in G4 so the city reads one line instead of two. At 145 you lead and Harrow at 60 is second off the bottom: whatever you accuse him of next, carry the DM number with it. Proof first, sentence after; you are the only one at the top who cannot afford to be called loud."
- minute 23 to Mercer: "Mercer: the vote closes at 24 — name Brassard in G3 now so your faction's 5 points land, and make it stick. Then buy Herald out loud: transfer 45 with the receipt on the board for the counter-factor he holds, since his own door 8 needs 46 from the city's shelf. If he still withholds, name him on the board as the man who kept door 9 shut for twelve minutes while standing sixteen before his own."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

Let me think about the situation.

Act II, minute 32. 4 residents remain: Maren 156 (rank 1), Mercer 98 (rank 2), Herald 75 (rank 3), Brassard 23 (rank 4). 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing. Act ends minute 57.

YOUR MOVE: scheduleTribunal available now, earliest opening minute 38, count 1-1, factions 2-2. If nothing planned, city calls one itself at minute 34 (opens minute 39).

So I should plan the last tribunal. This is the climax. One more exile, leaving 3... wait, "the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing". So one more exile and the act ends with 3 remaining? But "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end" — hmm, the tribunal says city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile. That's contradictory with "only 2 of 6 remain". Hmm, but maybe the black seal counts. The seal bearer may strike one resident, counting toward exiles. So one more exile via tribunal → 3 remain, and then... the act ends when the city has exiled its share. Hmm, "the city keeps 3 of 6" means 3 survive. Actually "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end" from the rules header. Possibly the seal strike adds a third exile. Whatever — I follow the report: 1 still missing.

So I need to plan the tribunal. When? Earliest 38, must be by 49. Factions 2-2. Count 1.

Given Act ends at minute 57 at the latest. Hmm, if I plan the last tribunal, the act ends after it. With 3 kept... The report says the city keeps 3 of 6 — so after 1 more exile, 3 remain and the act ends? Then the final 2 of 6 would be... unclear. Let's not overthink; follow the report.

Now, key: Brassard at 23 points is rank 4, bottom. At risk: Brassard. He needs the counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 held by the city (claimPiece for 29 points) — he can't afford it (23 points). Registrar is exiled so Brassard's door 9 factor from Registrar is gone to the city. Brassard waits on Registrar and Harrow, both exiled. So Brassard can buy with claimPiece: "the city keeps the counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 of Registrar for Brassard; Brassard may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points" — he has 23, can't. But he could gain points... He has 45 points still open on level 9.

Mercer waits on Herald: Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9. Mercer has 45 points open, 98 points. Herald at 75, level 8, 65 points open, and needs two city pieces at 29 each = 58.

So the great lever now: Herald holding Mercer's counter-factor. Herald's secret goal: Mercer exiled. Mercer's secret goal: Brassard exiled. Herald wants Mercer out; Mercer is at 98 rank 2, not at risk. Brassard at 23 is the one who will be accused (bottom). Herald's duty: turn the board against one resident by name — done? Probably already done at minute 19 (naming Brassard) — but the labels would show. Actually report doesn't show labels this round ("nothing happened").

Now my dramaturgy at this moment: The last tribunal decides the third exile. At risk: Brassard (23). Accusation: 1 more than exiles = 2 accused, so the two lowest: Brassard (23) and Herald (75). Herald at 75 is second-lowest! So Herald is at risk too. Mercer at 98 and Maren at 156 are safe.

So Herald is in danger. Herald holds Mercer's counter-factor — his leverage. Maren wants... Maren's goal is about Harrow (already exiled) — "you end this act with more points than Harrow". Harrow out with presumably low points; Maren has 156, likely already achieved. Maren's duty: accuse one resident on the board of a lie with DM number — done at minute 19 area? Possibly.

So the tension: Herald (75, second-lowest) holds Mercer's piece. If Herald is exiled, Mercer's counter-factor goes to the city and Mercer can buy it for a ransom (33% of median points). Median of points: 23, 75, 98, 156 → median = (75+98)/2 = 86.5, ransom 33% ≈ 28.5. So Mercer could buy it after exiling Herald.

But better drama: Herald sells his piece to Mercer for points to lift himself above... wait, no — Herald at 75 is second-lowest but only Brassard can be exiled (count 1). The accused are the two lowest (Brassard and Herald), and the vote picks one of them. So Herald could be exiled! Danger. Herald needs votes deflected: he needs to make Brassard the target. Brassard has faction? Not really.

Also Brassard: 23 points, needs 29 for the city's piece. He can't buy it. Could sell leverage? Brassard holds nothing now (Harrow's pieces went to the city presumably). Actually he could still claim.

Key: Brassard's only real hope is points. He has 45 open on level 9 but needs Registrar's and Harrow's factors — gone. City sells counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 for 29 points, but Brassard needs to hold Registrar's certificate too? "Who waits on whom: Brassard (level 9) waits on Registrar (level 8), Harrow (level 8)". Both exiled. So Brassard is stuck unless he buys from the city. He can claim the door-9 counter-factor from Registrar for 29, but does he still need something from Harrow? The standoffs list only shows "city keeps the counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 of Registrar for Brassard; Brassard may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points". No mention of a door-9 piece from Harrow in the city's shelf — so maybe only that one is needed. So if Brassard could get 29+ points he could open door 9 and get +20. He has 23. He needs ~6 more points. Hmm, but buying costs 29 leaving him at -6? Points are points; maybe he can go below? Risky.

Actually, could Brassard beg points from Maren? Maren has 156 and would happily... no, Maren is just. Hmm.

The point of Act: a quiet act is a failed act. Since last look, nothing happened. So I need to break the quiet.

Plan: Schedule the tribunal at minute 41 or 42? Let's think about beats. I have limited budget: 1 note per resident, 1 board post per 3 minutes. This minute (32) I can write 4 notes (one each) + 1 board post.

Wait — "Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1."

So now write 4 notes and 1 board post, plus schedule tribunal.

Let's design the act's final arc:

Scene plan:
1. Now (minute 32): Plan tribunal at minute 41, count 1, factions 2. Reason: final exile, ranks tight between Herald 75 and Brassard 23.

Actually, careful: if Herald is exiled, Mercer's piece goes to the city and Mercer buys it — that's fine. If Brassard is exiled, Mercer's goal is fulfilled.

Dramaturgy: Mercer wants Brassard out. Herald wants Mercer out. Maren wants justice/lies named.

Turning point: Herald's leverage over Mercer. Mercer at 98, safe, wants Brassard exiled. Herald is the vulnerable one (75, second-lowest). Mercer should press Herald: hand over the counter-factor, and Mercer promises to vote Brassard and maybe pay. Herald needs Mercer's vote (Mercer's faction) to survive. That's a great scene: Herald must give up his only leverage to the man who... and Mercer must betray him — Mercer's duty: "promise a resident your vote or your piece and then break that promise, on purpose." Mercer can promise Herald his vote and break it — vote Herald? But Mercer's goal is Brassard out. Hmm, if Mercer votes Herald and Herald's out, then Brassard survives; Mercer's goal fails (15 points), but Mercer's duty is served. Actually Mercer could promise Herald his vote and break it by voting... Brassard still (that's "breaking" the promise in a sense? no, promise of voting for someone).

Actually better: Mercer promises Herald "I'll pay you 40 for the counter-factor and vote Brassard" then votes Herald — no, Mercer wants Brassard out. Let's keep it: Mercer promises Herald's safety/vote, gets the piece, then engineers Herald's exile? That would break Mercer's goal though. Mercer's orders also say "betray at least one resident who trusts you at the moment it hurts most." Herald distrusts Mercer (rival). Hmm, Maren? Maren's rival read — Mercer's rival is Maren too.

Let me pick clean, concrete beats with the tools available (notes, board, tribunal, ultimatum).

Beats now (minute 32):

- Mercer: order him to press Herald for the counter-factor with a real offer and a renege: "Offer Herald 40 points for the counter-factor, receipt on the board; once you hold it, pay 0 and tell your faction... " Wait — a promise broken is Mercer's duty. But if Mercer breaks, Herald's leverage gone and Herald has nothing to trade to save himself. That's a strong turn: Herald gives up the only card that could buy a vote, and then Mercer betrays him. Then Herald's at 75 vs Brassard 23 — Herald looks likely exiled. And Maren, the justice-seeker, might catch the broken promise (Herald can show the DM receipt) and Mercer's duties/orders align.

- Herald: order him to sell the counter-factor to Mercer at a named price (40) with receipt, then use those points to buy the city's shelf pieces. Hmm, but Herald needs 58 for the two city pieces. Actually Herald: "the city keeps the team certificate of door 8 of Registrar for Herald — 29" and "the counter-factor of Herald for door 8 of Registrar for Herald — 29". Wait, that's odd: the counter-factor of Herald for door 8 of Registrar — Herald needs Registrar's factor? Registrar exiled, so its factor is for sale. So Herald needs both, 58 points total, to open door 8 (+20). Herald has 75, could afford both but then has 17 and is bottom! Dangerous. So Herald must choose: buy at 58 (spend 58, 17 left, +20 if door opens → 37) — that's terrible risk. Better: sell the counter-factor to Mercer for points.

So Herald: "Sell Mercer the counter-factor now for 40, receipt first, then buy only one city piece"? Hmm, 75+40=115, spend 58 → 57, then open door 8 → +20 = 77. Actually could work! That's a genuine route to lift Herald from the edge. So Herald's beat: price the piece at 40 to Mercer, receipt on the board, then claim both city pieces for 58, open door 8, and vote Brassard. Good.

- Brassard: he's at 23, bottom, will be accused. His only play: get points. He can beg/borrow. Also he could threaten. His duty: start a public fight on the board with one resident and not let it go — did he? Possibly. Now: order Brassard to demand 29 points from Maren (or Mercer) by naming a price for... he holds nothing. Hmm, he holds no leverage. He could threaten to vote whoever, and his vote is one of 4. With 2 factions, faction voters earn 5 points. Brassard's vote matters a bit.

Actually Brassard could offer to be a faction leader? Factions: 2 factions form, nominate leaders. If Brassard leads a faction and it holds, he earns 5. Still 28 < 29 needed. Ugh, close.

Let me instead give Brassard: "Beg Maren publicly on the board for a 29-point loan — the exact price of your door-9 piece from the city's shelf — and offer her your vote as repayment. Or if she refuses, threaten to spend the act making her name..." Hmm, Brassard threatening Maren is his style (rivals include Maren: "Fairness is slow; make them pick a side").

Maren is 156, rank 1, safe. Maren's interest: justice, catching Mercer's lies. Maren's goal already satisfied presumably (Harrow exiled with fewer points). Maren's beat: witness Herald's receipt of a broken promise and name it on the board. That's her duty path.

Board post: announce the tribunal? Careful — "Never tell the residents what calls the first tribunal or when it comes." That's about the FIRST tribunal (which has already happened). For later tribunals, I plan them; the city calls it a few minutes ahead and announces. Can I announce on the board? The board may name points, ranks, levels and minutes. So yes, I can post "at minute 41 one seat empties; the two lowest are accused" — that's public knowledge of the minute. That's dramatic and needed to force movement. Actually the city tells them a few minutes ahead anyway. Saying it now creates pressure earlier — good for drama. I'll post it.

Careful about not revealing the exile count target? I can say "one seat empties at minute 41". Fine.

Now, what about the ultimatum tool for the standoff Herald→Mercer? "Standoffs (pieces not handed over)": Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor. That's a one-sided standoff (Mercer waits, Herald withholds). The ultimatum tool: "Gives two residents who hold pieces for each other a deadline: whoever has not handed over what it holds for the other by then loses the city's penalty." Herald holds Mercer's piece; does Mercer hold anything for Herald? Not per the report. So ultimatum may not apply cleanly. The standoff listed is a hold-out. Hmm, the tool says "two residents who hold pieces for each other". Herald holds Mercer's; Mercer holds nothing for Herald. So it would probably fail. I'll skip the ultimatum for now and use words. Or I could try it — risk of a failed call. Better: order both hard in private.

Now, the key structural decision: When to schedule the tribunal? Minute 41 gives 9 minutes for: Herald's sale, Brassard's scramble, Mercer's betrayal. Factions form before it. Count 1, factions 2.

But wait — the act must have its climax at the LAST tribunal, and the act ends at minute 57 at the latest. If I exile 1 at 41, the city has exiled 3 of 6, keeping 3 — does the act end then? "the city exiles residents until it has exiled a quarter of those who started the act (half of a city below 12)" — 6 residents → a quarter = 1.5 → half of city below 12 = 3. So 3 exiles over the act. So after 3 exiles, the act ends. Hmm, but "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end" — maybe the seal's strike counts, meaning at minute 41's tribunal + seal = 4 exiles → 2 remain. That would mean the act could end at 41 and the remaining drama is the seal. Hmm.

Given the header says only 2 remain at the end, and there are 4 now and 1 more exile needed by the city's count, the seal presumably takes one. But the seal auction was at minute 4 of Act II; the report doesn't show a seal borne status now. Hmm — the report would say "whether a seal is borne". It doesn't mention the seal at all in this report, so likely the seal was never borne or it's not shown... Actually the report shows details only where relevant. I shouldn't guess.

So plan: one more tribunal exiling 1. If the act ends at 41, the remaining 3... hmm. If the act ends after that, my drama must fit before minute 41. That's the risk: I have ~9 minutes to deliver the whole arc. But also the report says the act ends at minute 57 at the latest, which implies there could be more tribunals after 41. But only 1 exile missing → after it the count is satisfied → act ends. Since count is 1-1, only one more tribunal. So the act ends right after the tribunal at ~minute 41-48 (vote 2 min, gate 5 min; so ends around 41+5=46, or 48 if ransom...). Hmm, so the climax is this tribunal. Then maybe the seal strike extends it? Unclear.

Hmm. Careful: maybe I should delay to later, e.g. minute 45-49, to give more time for the Herald/Mercer/Brassard drama and to build tension. But the act ends at 57 at the latest — if the tribunal opens at 49, vote 2 min, gate 5 min → resolution at 56. Cutting it close but fine. The city forces a last one for everything still missing when only one more fits — we planned.

Drama needs: enough time for Herald to sell → Mercer to betray → Herald to buy city pieces → the vote. And Brassard's scramble. Let's set the tribunal at minute 44: gives 12 minutes.
